items.title: Understanding Tenth Parts in Measurement
items.explanation: To measure objects accurately, we use smaller units like tenths (1/10th of a unit). For example, if a pencil is 3.4 units long, it means 3 full units plus 4 one-tenths. This helps us break down large measurements into manageable parts for precise reading.

items.title: Adding and Subtracting One-Tenth Units
items.explanation: When adding or subtracting lengths with fractional units, it is easier to convert everything to tenths first. For instance, 2.7 + 3.6 becomes (2+3) + (0.7+0.6) = 5 + 1.3 = 6.3 one-tenths, which equals 6 units and 3 one-tenths.

items.title: Finding Differences in Lengths
items.explanation: To find the difference between two lengths, subtract the smaller from the larger while handling tenths carefully. For example, if Shylaja's head is 2.3 units and thorax is 5.4 units, the total length is found by combining these fractional parts.
